citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., and Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843.
creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher (MetaMind - A Salesforce Company)
description: WikiText is a language modeling benchmark dataset constructed from Wikipedia articles that passed the Good or Featured article criteria. It is available in two sizes: WikiText-2 (approximately twice the size of Penn Treebank, ~2M tokens) and WikiText-103 (over 103 million tokens from all extracted articles). Both feature punctuation, original casing, a larger vocabulary, and numbers, enabling evaluation of long-range dependencies and rare word handling.
name: WikiText
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is constructed exclusively from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles, which are reviewed and curated by Wikipedia editors. This selection criterion may introduce bias toward well-written, encyclopedic content and may not reflect the full diversity of natural language use. The paper also notes that other large-scale datasets have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering, motivating this construction choice.
rai:dataCollection: Articles were selected from Wikipedia that met the Good or Featured article criteria as specified by Wikipedia editors. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. Text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw text extracted from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles via the Wikipedia API. The raw Wikipedia markup contains macros used for metric conversion, abbreviations, language notation, and date handling.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is derived only from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles, which may not be representative of all language use. The paper notes that the dataset is about a tenth the size of the One Billion Word Benchmark.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Specific sections primarily featuring lists were removed. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from HTML were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (e.g., 8,600 → 8 @,@ 600). A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3; words outside the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable more realistic language modeling research by providing a freely available benchmark with larger vocabulary, original casing, punctuation, and longer documents compared to the Penn Treebank. This supports research on rare word prediction and long-term dependency modeling.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark dataset for word-level language modeling, particularly for evaluating models on longer-range dependencies, realistic vocabularies with rare words, and named entity prediction. Intended as a replacement for the Penn Treebank for language modeling research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007) was used for normalization and tokenization, slightly augmented to further split numbers.

null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform used; dataset was constructed automatically.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol; dataset is a text corpus extracted and preprocessed automatically.

null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection manipulation (augmentation, balancing, resampling) described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described in the paper.
